title: Sicilian-Style Thick Pan Pizza with Onion, Tomato and Crisp Crumbs
summary: A soft, airy semolina dough topped with sweet, slowly cooked onion and tomato and finished with a crisp layer of pecorino-style cheese breadcrumbs and oregano. Baked in a tin and cut into generous squares.
equipment: 23 x 33 cm metal baking tin or rimmed tray

ingredients.item: plain flour (or tipo 00), plus extra for dusting
fine sea salt or table salt
large onion, halved and thinly sliced
fine sea salt or table salt
pecorino-style hard cheese (microbial rennet), finely grated

steps.title: Mix and chill dough
steps.text: Stir the yeast and semolina into the lukewarm water and leave for 5 minutes, until bubbly. Add the flour, salt and the 2 tbsp dough oil, then knead for 5 minutes until smooth and soft, adding only a little flour so it stays soft. Cover and chill for at least 2 hours and up to 24 hours; the cool rest makes the dough easier to handle and builds flavour.

steps.title: Soften the onion
steps.text: Heat the 2 tbsp topping oil in the frying pan over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until translucent. Pour in the 100ml water, turn up the heat and bubble for about 5 minutes, until the water has gone and the onion is very soft. Cooking it in water first makes it sweet and tender without browning.

steps.title: Simmer the topping
steps.text: Stir in the passata, salt, pepper and chilli and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick, then leave to cool. A thick, cool topping will not soak into the soft dough.

steps.title: Mix the crumbs
steps.text: Combine the breadcrumbs, pecorino-style cheese, 1 tbsp oil and oregano. The oil coats the crumbs so they toast to a golden crunch in the oven.

steps.title: Stretch into the tin
steps.text: Oil the tin with 2 tbsp of the tin oil. Flatten the cold dough with the rolling pin into a small rectangle, lay it in the tin and press it out to the edges with your palms, resting it for 5 minutes if it springs back. Cover with the tea towel and leave somewhere warm for 30-45 minutes, until about doubled in thickness.

steps.title: Preheat the oven
steps.text: Heat the oven to 200°C (fan 180°C), with the shelf in the middle, for at least 20 minutes before baking. A moderate oven cooks the thick dough right through before the topping over-browns.

steps.title: Top the dough
steps.text: Spread the cooled onion and tomato over the dough, leaving a 1cm border. Scatter the crumbs evenly over the top and drizzle with the last 1 tbsp tin oil.

steps.title: Bake until crisp
steps.text: Bake for 30-35 minutes, until the crumbs are golden and the base is browned and crisp; lift a corner with the spatula to check and give it 5 minutes more if pale. Cover loosely with foil if the top browns too fast. Rest for 5 minutes, then slide it out and cut into 8 squares, serving warm or at room temperature.

tips: A common mistake is adding too much flour while kneading, which makes the crumb dense; keep the dough soft and slightly sticky.
Let the topping cool completely before spreading, or the warm sauce can deflate the risen dough.
Check the base before taking it out, as a pale underside will turn soggy once it cools.
Use finely grated pecorino-style cheese so it blends with the crumbs into an even, crunchy layer.
storage: Cool leftovers within 2 hours and refrigerate for up to 3 days. Reheat in a hot oven or a dry frying pan until piping hot (74°C).
